neighbours.label: subject pronoun ('you', 'they') of a wh-question put to the listener ('what do you think', 'how would you')
fire: We tried three different paint colors in the hallway. Which one do you like best?
The menu changed again this spring. What did you order the last time you came in?
My tomatoes keep splitting before they ripen. How would you handle that?
Thanks for joining us on the podcast today. So how did you first get into pottery?
Your team switched to a four-day week last year. What have they noticed since then?
Lots of readers wrote in about the finale. What did you all make of that ending?
Before we wrap up the interview, where do you see the company in five years?
You both run marathons, right? How do you train during the winter months?
quiet: We tried three different paint colors in the hallway, and I suspect you will like the blue one.
The menu changed again this spring, so you might find your usual dish is gone.
My tomatoes keep splitting before they ripen, and you told me that happens after heavy rain.
Thanks for joining us on the podcast today; you have been making pottery for twenty years.
Your team switched to a four-day week last year, and they noticed fewer sick days since then.
Lots of readers wrote in about the finale, and you all seemed to hate that ending.
Before we wrap up the interview, I want to thank you for your time and your candor.
You both run marathons, and you train indoors during the winter months.

notes: Card: ' you' x19, ' they' x4, all right after 'what do/would/have' in interview-style questions. Near misses keep 'you' as a subject in statements.
